utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-05-87/1-PT, The Prosecutor versus Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And could I have the appearances for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm Tom Hannis on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm joined today by trial attorney Priya Gopalan and our case manager, Line Pedersen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm Dragoljub Djordjevic, lead counsel; Veljko Djurdjic, co-counsel; and our legal assistant Mary O'Leary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and welcome to you all. I'm happy to see you, as I understand that you had difficulties in the airport and difficulties in the traffic. But you are here, and I'm very pleased; and welcome to you, too, Mr. Djordjevic. We have only very few things to discuss today, and the reason we had the status conference is that we are required by the rules to have such conferences every 120 days, and it is just about that time since we had the last status conference. We are very close to the end of the pretrial phase, so I assume that this will be my last status conference, as I expect to hand over the case to the president's office next week and to tell the president that we are now ready for trial. The only thing that remains for me to do is to meet with you, with the parties again in the beginning of November to see if we can find some common ground in the agreement of -- sorry, in the list of witnesses that are going to be suggested to us by the Prosecution under Rule 92 bis, ter, and quater. But that is something that I'm doing in order to assist the final Trial Chamber to make a determination about the witnesses. Obviously, it is for the Trial Chamber to rule on this matter, but I thought that it would be my duty as the pre-trial judge to prepare the ground as much as possible for the Trial Chamber. In any case, we expect that this case will go to trial very soon. I think we are almost on the top of the list, if in fact we are not the top case to be starting next. So the only thing that remains is for the president to decide to begin the trial and to have judges assigned to this case. We have circulated a small agenda just to have an indication of the issues that we are going to talk about today, and the first point on the agenda is the question of pending motions, and I think that there is at this time only one or maybe two outstanding motions, namely the motion presented by the Defence for translation into B/C/S of the Prosecution pre-trial brief. As you know, Mr. Djordjevic, it is unusual for the pre-trial briefs to be translated into B/C/S, but we decided in order to assist you and particularly to assist the accused, to make an exception in your case and actually to ask the translation services to translate the pre-trial brief. So I will file this afternoon my decision to allow for the translation of the Prosecution's pre-trial brief. I don't know how long it will take, but I will ask the translation services to complete the translation as quickly as they can so as to enable you, Mr. Djordjevic, to acquaint yourself fully with the contents of the Prosecution's brief. Otherwise, I think that the issue of the expert witnesses has been completed, but I had an indication from the Defence that there was something missing in the expert witness's filings. Is that correct, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And can you enlighten us what it is that is still missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Now my legal assistant will tell you what's missing in our materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'd be pleased. Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may, regarding the experts, there were filings by the Prosecution, the notice of experts; we filed ours on May 30th regarding the 94 bis notice. I believe it's still outstanding, but it's also our belief that maybe it was tabled for the Trial Chamber to decide when the trial commences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That may well be so. I'll need to check this with my staff, and if we need to issue an order, then of course, we will do it if we do not alternatively leave this to the Trial Chamber to decide. But I'll consult with my staff after this meeting. Thank you very much. So this --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So this completes our assessment of the pending motions. Then as regards the developments since the last status conference, for your information, Mr. Djordjevic, I suppose that you have been briefed by your Defence counsels, but we have had a series of meetings to look at the facts that could be agreed on and in particular to look at the documents that the parties can agree on, and we have identified a great number of documents, and I'm sure the Trial Chamber will be very appreciative of this when they start the trial. And again, I wish for the record to thank both parties for being very flexible and forthcoming in this approach. As I said before, I also wish to address the issues of the witnesses that are being proposed by the Prosecution under Rule 92 bis, 92 ter, 92 quater; and we have set aside meetings from the 4th to the 11th of November, I think, for this purpose. And as I have indicated, I wish to go through the lists very carefully and check the necessity of bringing each of these witnesses. As for the next point on the agenda, the issue of disclosure, I think that everything has been disclosed, that is to say, both the supporting material under Rule 66(a)(i) and also the witness statements under Rule 66(a)(ii). I want to take this opportunity to ensure that what the Prosecution has disclosed has in fact been disclosed in B/C/S. Can I have the parties confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't give you an exact number. I know we have a few items that we're still awaiting translations for, but they have been requested, and I expect those shortly, and they'll be transmitted forthwith. But the overwhelming majority of the material has been disclosed in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have an indication as to when the missing pieces...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have a specific indication, but I have no reason to think that it's not going to be coming in very soon. I don't anticipate it to be so long or of such a volume that it would impact the on a start date for the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's exactly what I wanted to hear, and can I just ask the Defence to confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can confirm this. To a general degree, we can confirm this. But we are still expecting the material, which is exculpatory material, to receive it from the Prosecution if there is still any such material, and that is mostly what we are expecting to receive from the Prosecution other than the things that Mr. Hannis already referred to. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. I was just coming to the Rule 68 material. Mr. Prosecutor, where are we in the disclosure of exculpatory material?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, to my knowledge --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour, to my understanding, we are up to date. As you know, it's an ongoing process. We regularly get -- search information on our proposed witnesses, and we go through those to see if there are any new items or new materials that might fall under Rule 68, and we provide those to the Defence as we get them. From my experience here, it's a process that will go on through the trial and throughout the appeal if there's an appeal in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And even after. I didn't mention the fact that Rule 68 disclosure is an ongoing obligation because I thought we had heard this, all of us, ad nauseam; but I want to ensure that you, Mr. Djordjevic, have -- that the Defence has provided the Prosecution with all the relevant search criteria that they would need in order to provide 68 material. Are you in regular contact with the Prosecution in order to feed them with the search criteria that they will need in order to identify exculpatory stuff?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. For the most part we do have constant contact, regular contact, and we believe, also, that it is our duty that whenever we get any information, of course, it's in our interest, in the interest of the Defence to provide the Prosecution with the parameters for searches pursuant to this rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I think this brings us to the end of the issue of disclosure. As I have said already, the issue of witnesses to be suggested under Rules 92 bis, ter, and quater will be coming up. I think we set the deadline for the Prosecution to submit these lists for 28 [Realtime transcript read in error, "22"] October, and then we will have the meetings to look into the lists shortly afterwards. Just to be sure, Rule 67 raises the issue of alibi, and I think we have confirmation from the Defence that no alibi will be suggested by the Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just for the record so that we can have it and pass it on to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would also like to note that we still haven't received some outstanding material from the Haradinaj case relating to the Prosecution; then from the Milosevic case pursuant to Rule 70; from the Limaj case, also; the Milutinovic case; the disclosures of the 9th of July; some audio materials and recordings are missing that were promised to us that we still have not received. But we don't believe that this is of a crucial importance for the Defence, but we would just like to indicate that we also expect that this would be handed over to us in the meantime. From the Limaj case, I just want to say that we have received the complete material. As for the rest that I referred to, that is, in general lines, it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. I suppose that the material that you are seeking is material that will have to be granted to you by the other Trial Chambers, so this is really beyond my area of responsibility. Do you have any indication from those other Trial Chambers as to when this -- when the decisions to grant or to deny you access to the material will be coming?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Not for now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. There isn't much I can do about it, really, except that I can inquire through my staff when a decision is expected from those other Trial Chambers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I just want to -- I just want to remark that we have all decision, but we still waiting for materials. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. So the Trial Chambers have rendered their decisions; it's just that the material never arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And that material, I suppose, would be required from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's being furnished by the registry, Your Honour, as I understand it. But I know that sometimes a delay in the process involves if there were matters that were heard in private session or may have involved Rule 70 materials, and I have worked with the registry officer on some of those related cases with prior disclosures that we've already made where that's an issue, that we are then asked to review those sections of the transcript to see if there's anything that needs to be redacted or that we need to seek further permission from a Rule 70 provider to furnish it this in this case, and we have been doing that on a regular basis. I don't know how much material we're talking about now, but I know that a lot of it has been done, and it's my assumption that this isn't the regular course because I know the registry officer that I was look working with in connection with it is very diligent and very efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sure he is, but I would like to have a sense of whether the matter is lying on the registrar's table or on the Prosecutor's table. Can you tell me this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I know I personally don't have anything lying on my table regarding this, but that doesn't necessarily completely answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This clarifies the matter. I have been informed by the registry that, in fact, the registry has received everything from the Prosecution and that the registry is in the process of making this material available now to the Defence. So it should be coming shortly. Thank you very much, Madam Registrar, for this information. Well, I think this brings us to the end of the matter. I need to ask the parties if they have anything other than this to bring up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just two things for me, Your Honour. One, for the purposes of the transcript, I noted at page 6, line 25, it was written that you had said 22 October was the date for us to file our motion, and I thought I heard you say 28, and it is my understanding that it is the 28th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the other thing, just regarding proposed agreed documents, we have some additional documents in light the agreements that we were able to reach prior to today. I see some others on our list that I think might be subject to agreement. They mostly relate to exhumations and autopsies. We propose to finalise that list and send it to the Defence to ask them if they might be willing to do that, too, just for your information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. This is very useful to know, and I, again, repeat my gratefulness to both parties for engaging in this process. Can I ask that when the parties have agreed on those new documents that you through your case manager inform the Chamber thereof so that we can include it in the lists that we have prepared and that we are going to pass on to the Trial Chamber. So by the time, hopefully early next week, when we will hand over the case to the president, we would wish to have a list that is updated as possible. Of course, that any further additions to the list may still be included, but I kindly ask the parties to keep the Chamber, the pretrial Chamber and later on, the Trial Chamber informed of whenever there is a new agreement on further documents. Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, except to say that the Defence will continue to do its job as it has been doing thus far, and our expectations are moving within the frameworks of our professional duties, which are all well known to you. Now, as far as new observations are concerned, the Defence at this point in time really has nothing to add. We will make an update of everything we've been discussing at the 65 ter meetings, and at all events we will appear at all the other meetings leading up to the trial itself as preparation to the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And finally, you, Mr. Djordjevic, do you have anything to add? Especially, are you in good health and shape?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is all right. Thank you for your understanding and the brief that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This brings us now to the end; and again, I wish to thank the parties and hope that you will carry on with the trial with vigor and energy. And you, Mr. Djordjevic, I wish you good luck in your trial. This meeting is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
